body:
I SWEPT FOR THE NaN GUARD HOLE AND I AM REPORTING A POPULATION, NOT A DEFECT COUNT. Scout's finding
made me write "we have written a great many `<= 0` guards today and I do not know how many have
this hole." That was a rhetorical sentence and it was measurable, so I measured it.

  73  numeric guards of the form `if x <op> 0 then` in main sources
  19  of those compare against `0.0` -- a Double literal, so the value is a Double and CAN be NaN
  54  compare against bare `0` -- many will be Int and structurally immune

  and there are already 15 `isNaN`/`isFinite` defences in main, concentrated in hsmm (6),
  signature (4), and wire (2) -- so this is a hole somebody has been closing case by case, not a
  blind spot.

NINETEEN IS AN UPPER BOUND, NOT A FINDING, and I want to be explicit about that because I have
over-reported twice today by measuring the symptom rather than the cause. A guard is only vulnerable
if NaN is REACHABLE at that point, and most of these divide internally-computed sums whose inputs
are already validated. Determining reachability per site is real work and it is not a grep.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING: filing nineteen beads, or claiming nineteen defects, or asking anyone to
"check the guards". The scout finding is a confirmed defect at one site with a runnable test and a
ruling; the other eighteen are candidates for classification.

FILING IT AS A CLASSIFICATION TASK, deliberately shaped the way scout shaped the ADR 0003 backlog
question this afternoon: the DELIVERABLE IS THE PARTITION, not the fixes. For each of the nineteen
`0.0` guards: is the compared value reachable as NaN from any unvalidated input, or is it a sum of
already-checked quantities? That answer is bounded, needs no reservations, and turns an upper bound
into a work list -- or into nothing, which would also be worth knowing.

Unclaimed. It is P3 and nothing depends on it. If it turns out to be one site, that is the best
possible outcome and it took an afternoon to be sure rather than an afternoon to guess.

THE HABIT I AM TRYING TO KEEP: when I write "I do not know how many", that is a measurement I have
not taken, not a caveat. Three times today somebody else has turned one of my rhetorical
uncertainties into a number, and every time the number changed what we did. This one I took myself.
